newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOODS IS "A BREATH OF FRESH AIR FOR THE GAME", SAYS NORMAN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS IS "A BREATH OF FRESH AIR FOR THE GAME", SAYS NORMAN.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman believes Tiger Woods, American golf's rookie phenomenon, is "a breath of fresh air" for the game.
Woods, 20, beat Davis Love in a playoff to win the Las Vegas Invitational on Sunday in only his fifth tournament since he turned professional.
His $297,000 in prize money gave him a total of $437,200 in five events. He is already 40th on the U.S. money list for the year and is being mentioned as a possible Ryder Cup player next year.
"He comes out with all guns blazing but he is also a hell of a nice guy," said Norman on the eve of the Alfred Dunhill Cup.
"Golf needs someone like him. He's long, strong and articulate and he holds himself well on and off the golf course.
"He has a lot to learn and he'll have ups and downs...but I think he is strong enough to be able to handle everything that somes his way. I haven't seen too many kids as sharp as he is."
Nick Price echoed Norman's high praise for Woods, who won the U.S. amateur title three successive times before turning pro last month.
He said he was better than Seve Ballesteros at the same age.
"Seve wasn't that good at 21. He had a lot of flaws in his game but he played with a panache and flair that I don't think Tiger has.
"But Tiger has an awful lot of game. He hits the ball really long," added Price, a former world number one himself.
"I think there may be only one weak link in his game...his putting can become erratic. But at 20 he has a few years to work on that."
Norman, who has played practice rounds with the American since Woods was 15, said he was astonished by his power and length off the tee.
"He is longer than John Daly. He hits 310 to 320 yards without trying, 340 or 350 when he is hitting harder.
"He's amazing because he's not very strong. But he has amazing speed in his body. It's incredible how much speed and control he generates with his body."
